subject: Partial degradation on hosted inference (edge routing) — customer advisory
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.health>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.health>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: [URGENT] 503s across ~30% of inference calls (examples attached)

Hi Sergio,

We started seeing a burst of 503 errors hitting our inference endpoints around 07:50 ET this morning. ~30% of requests are returning 503 or timing out with request_id examples attached (request-debug-sample.txt). The failures are concentrated on short chat-like calls (max_tokens 256) but appear across multiple model routes.

This is impacting our user flows — sessions are getting dropped and retries make the experience jittery. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something in our routing? We rely on your hosted offering for production so any ETA would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Samir
Lead SRE, Brightline Health

Attachments: request-debug-sample.txt (text), example-logs-snippet.txt (text)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.health>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:25:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 503s across ~30% of inference calls (examples attached)

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the request IDs. We see a correlated spike in 5xx responses on our edge routing plane originating from the us-east-1 edge tier starting at ~07:48 ET.

What we're doing now:
- Triage: routing team (Grace + Aditya) investigating immediate root cause (suspected routing fanout to a saturated replica group).
- Mitigation: preparing a traffic-shift plan to route affected customers away from the impacted edge nodes into warm fallback capacity.
- Communication: I’ve opened an incident on our status page (INC-20261210-edge-routing). URL: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261210-edge-routing

Can you do a quick smoke test (same request IDs) in ~15 mins and tell us whether errors persist? We'll follow up with a targeted mitigation within the hour and keep you updated.

Apologies for the disruption — I know this affects your customers.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

[Internal note: Grace, Aditya — assigning to you to confirm whether this is a routing plane fanout issue or KV eviction cascade on the edge. Priority P1. — SA]
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.health>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Update: partial restoration in progress / targeted traffic shift applied

Samir — quick update: we applied a targeted traffic-shift at 08:58 ET that routed your traffic (and other affected tenants) away from the saturated us-east-1 edge nodes into warm fallback pools in us-east-2. Early telemetry shows a significant drop in 5xx rates for the routed tenants.

What changed:
- Implemented routing override + drain on suspect nodes (08:58 ET)
- Increased warm pool capacity for the us-east region (09:00 ET)
- Enabled more aggressive request queuing (short window) to avoid head-of-line blocking during the drain

Observed impact so far:
- Error rate for Brightline's example request IDs dropped from ~32% -> ~4% within 5 minutes of the shift.
- A small subset of requests still returns transient 503; we are continuing the drain and will keep your traffic on the fallback pools until we confirm stability.

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.pdf (contains traffic-shift steps and rollback knobs)

Next steps:
- Can you rerun the failing flows and report results? If you continue to see >5% errors we’ll escalate to full region failover.
- We will keep the override in place for 2 hours for evaluation and then begin a controlled rehydration once confident.

Thanks for your patience. I’ll send a post-incident follow-up with root cause and permanent mitigations.

— Sergio
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.health>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Post-incident: edge-routing partial degradation — summary & next steps

Hi Samir — following up with a short post-incident summary and next steps. We kept the traffic override in place for ~3 hours and completed controlled rehydration overnight; traffic to the affected nodes has been stable since ~02:10 ET.

Preliminary findings (full postmortem in drive):
- Root cause: an unexpected routing table refresh combined with a recent change to our edge autoscaler logic resulted in temporary fanout to a subset of replicas that had stale KV cache entries. That combination led to saturation and elevated 5xx for a subset of edge nodes.
- Impact window: 07:48 ET — 02:10 ET (partial degradation, peak 5xx ~32% for some tenants).
- Scope: affected tenants routed through the us-east-1 edge tier (includes Brightline).

Action items we’re tracking (owners):
1) Revert/patch autoscaler condition to prevent aggressive replica fanout (Aditya) — ETA: 48h
2) Add a routing-plane canary that simulates KV freshness checks prior to routing changes (Grace) — ETA: 72h
3) Improve statuspage automation to reflect affected tenant lists (Sergio) — ETA: 24h
4) Provide Brightline with an ops playbook for client-side graceful retry/backoff knobs (Evelyn) — ETA: 72h

Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/postmortems/INC-20261210-edge-routing-postmortem
Incident on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261210-edge-routing
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BRG-ENTERPRISE-2025-41

If you’d like a walkthrough of the postmortem or prefer a short ops sync with our routing team, I can set that up for early next week. Appreciate your patience and the quick debug samples — those made the triage much faster.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
